fichas.title: Electronic locking and identification systems
fichas.summary: Electronic locking components are arranged according to security requirements: sensor and control are separated for high-security situations, but may be combined where access control is supervised. Identification systems include contact and contactless electronic media, as well as biometric identification and verification. Access rights can be managed electronically, and systems may connect to central monitoring.

fichas.title: Mechanical and key locking systems
fichas.summary: Mechanical cylinder locks provide security and may be extended to suit door thickness. Locking systems use an associated security certificate for replacement keys. Central locking systems allow one key to operate a flat entrance door and shared doors, while hierarchical master-key systems organize access rights across multiple cylinders. Electronic systems can change access rights without replacing building components.

fichas.title: Emergency exits, panic doors, and break-in risk
fichas.summary: Emergency exits serve buildings or areas not open to the public, where occupants familiar with the location understand the escape-door function. Panic doors serve public buildings or areas where users may not understand that function. Emergency-exit and panic-door ironmongery must be tested, approved, and labelled as a complete system. The page also groups doors and other building components by break-in risk according to use.
